slides.headline: Train for the trail on the reformer
slides.sub: How Pilates builds the balance and control that hills and rocky tracks ask for.

slides.title: Single-leg strength matters
slides.body: Every step on a trail is a small single-leg balance exercise. Pilates work like single-leg footwork, reformer lunges and side-lying series builds strength one leg at a time.

slides.title: Control on the way down
slides.body: Downhills need your quads and glutes to work while they lengthen. Slow, controlled returns of the carriage train that braking skill, which can make long descents feel more manageable.

slides.title: Ankles that react
slides.body: Balance work, heel raises and footwork on the footbar can help your ankles adjust to rocks and tree roots. Many people notice steadier footing after a few weeks of regular practice.

slides.title: A trunk that carries a pack
slides.body: A day pack adds load to your back and shoulders. Exercises for the trunk, upper back and hips help you carry it comfortably for hours without slumping over by lunch.

slides.title: Plan your build-up
slides.body: Two sessions a week alongside regular walks on hills and stairs is a practical starting point. Start several weeks before a big hike, rather than the week before, so your body can adapt.

slides.headline: Big walk on the calendar?
slides.body: Our clinical Pilates team at Hybrid Physiotherapy assesses your balance, strength and history, then builds a program around your hiking plans. Book online, link in bio.

caption:
Planning a big hike this summer? Your legs will thank you for some reformer time first.

Trails ask for single-leg strength, ankles that react to rocks and roots, and quads that can control long descents. Clinical Pilates trains all of that with slow, controlled work on the reformer and mat.

A practical starting point is two sessions a week alongside regular hill and stair walks, beginning several weeks out. That gives your body time to adapt to the load before the big day.

Our clinical Pilates team at Hybrid Physiotherapy can build a program around your plans. Book online via the link in bio.
